CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left wrist pain and numbness with tingling in left hand.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
George presents with a several-month history of left wrist pain and left hand numbness and tingling affecting all fingers, with predominance in the thumb and index finger, and occasional involvement of the fifth finger. Symptoms began insidiously without known precipitating factor. Pain and numbness are worse at night, and he frequently wakes with the left hand asleep, requiring him to shake it out to restore sensation. He reports associated grip weakness in the left hand and has been dropping things due to difficulty sensing them in his hand. He denies right hand involvement. Patient works in landscaping and yard maintenance, performing heavy labor with repetitive movements including raking and digging. He drinks approximately 1-2 beers on weekends (Friday and Saturday). Denies prior diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for left hand numbness, tingling, and weakness. Negative for right hand involvement, rheumatoid arthritis, or constitutional symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None documented.

MEDICATIONS
None documented.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupation: Landscaping and yard work maintenance with heavy labor and repetitive motions. Alcohol: 1-2 beers on weekends. Tobacco and other substance use: Not documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert and oriented. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Upper extremities: Grip strength decreased on left compared to right. Sensation to touch intact in fingers, though patient notes sensation feels different on thumb side compared to pointer finger. Tinel's sign positive bilaterally at wrist with jolt/zing sensation elicited in fingertips with percussion.

RESULTS
EMG study ordered; results pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, predominantly left-sided, likely related to occupational repetitive stress from landscaping work. Plan: (1) Activity modification—delegate heavy repetitive work to other employees for 2 weeks to eliminate repetitive motions; (2) Left wrist splint; (3) Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours; (4) EMG study ordered to assess electrical impulses to fingers; (5) Follow-up office visit in 2 weeks to assess response to conservative treatment; (6) Discussed possible surgical intervention (carpal tunnel release) if conservative treatment fails or if EMG results indicate need.
